beats.text: Before roads, every rainy day turned travel into a mud trap.
Over five thousand years ago, Mesopotamian cities began paving their streets with stone.
The Romans went further: layers of sand, gravel and fitted stone, curved so the rain ran off.
They built over eighty thousand kilometers of paved roads.
In the 1820s, John McAdam packed crushed stone into one tight, smooth layer.
Then in 1902, Edgar Hooley sealed it with tar, and tarmac was born.
Today, highways stack thick layers of asphalt and concrete, carrying millions of cars every day.
Follow to see how everything evolved.
